question: Following the martyrdom of numerous Huffaz (memorizers of the Qur'an) at the Battle of Yamamah, which companion advised Caliph Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Holy Qur'an into a single codex?
explanation: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) grew deeply concerned over the loss of memorizers at Yamamah and urged Caliph Abu Bakr (RA) to commission the compilation of the scattered Qur'anic manuscripts.

question: Which prominent companion was appointed by Caliph Abu Bakr (RA) as the head of the committee tasked with collecting the written fragments of the Holy Qur'an?
explanation: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA), the Prophet's chief scribe, was selected for his exceptional memorization, writing skill, integrity, and firsthand knowledge of the revelations.

question: During whose Caliphate was the official standardized text (Mushaf) of the Holy Qur'an copied into the Quraysh dialect and dispatched to major Islamic provinces to eradicate dialectical discrepancies?
explanation: Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (RA) unified the Muslim Ummah upon a single standardized orthographic reading (Mushaf al-Uthmani) based on the dialect of Quraysh.

question: In the science of Tajweed, when a Nun Sakinah or Tanween is immediately followed by one of the six throat letters (Hamzah, Ha, 'Ayn, Haa, Ghayn, Kha), the rule applied is ______
explanation: Izhar Halqi entails pronouncing the Nun Sakinah or Tanween clearly and distinctly without elongation or extra nasalization (ghunnah).

question: The phonetic transformation of a Nun Sakinah or Tanween into a sound of 'Mim' with ghunnah when followed by the letter 'Ba' is known as ______
explanation: Iqlab literally means turning or converting; it changes the Nun Sakinah into an unwritten Mim before the letter Ba (e.g., 'Mim-ba'di').

question: The echoing or bouncing acoustic articulation produced when pronouncing any of the letters of 'Qutbu Jaddin' (Qaf, Ta, Ba, Jeem, Dal) with a Sukun is called ______
explanation: Qalqalah refers to the vibration or bouncing resonance that occurs when releasing one of the five letters of Qutbu Jadd while carrying a Sukun.

question: In Surah Luqman (31:13), what did Luqman describe as the greatest injustice or monumental transgression (Zulmun Azeem) when advising his son?
explanation: Luqman admonished his son: 'O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice (Zulmun Azeem)'.

question: According to Surah Luqman (31:18-19), which social behavioral conduct is explicitly condemned when Luqman warns against turning one's cheek in contempt?
explanation: Luqman advised his son not to turn his face away from people in arrogance, nor walk haughtily on the earth, for Allah does not love the arrogant boaster.

question: In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:6), what guideline are believers commanded to observe when an untrustworthy person or evil-doer (Faasiq) brings them information?

options.a: Verify and investigate the news carefully before acting
options.b: Reject the news outright without investigation
options.c: Punish the person immediately with lashes
options.d: Spread the information to alert others

explanation: The Qur'an mandates: 'O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate (verify), lest you harm a people out of ignorance...'

question: In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:12), the vile sin of backbiting (Gheebah) against fellow Muslims is vividly compared to ______

options.a: Eating the flesh of one's dead brother
options.c: Setting one's own house on fire

explanation: The verse asks: 'Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his brother when dead? You would detest it.' (Surah Al-Hujurat 49:12).

question: According to Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13), what is the sole criterion of nobility and superiority in the sight of Allah among diverse nations and tribes?
explanation: The verse establishes: 'Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you (Atqaakum)'. Race, ethnicity, and status confer no merit.

question: The infamous incident in Islamic history involving malicious slander against the character of Ummul Mu'minin Aisha (RA), which was divinely refuted in Surah An-Nur, is known as ______
explanation: The Incident of the Slander (Hadith al-Ifk) was orchestrated by the hypocrites led by Abdullah ibn Ubayy, following which Allah revealed ten verses in Surah An-Nur completely exonerating Aisha (RA).

question: Which revered verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (verse 255) is acclaimed as the greatest single verse of the Holy Qur'an, celebrating Allah's absolute sovereignty, life, and preservation of the universe?
explanation: Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne, 2:255) explicitly proclaims Tawheed, Allah's eternal living nature (Al-Hayy, Al-Qayyum), and His omnipotent dominion.

question: In the formal science of Hadith (Mustalah al-Hadith), the continuous uninterrupted chronological chain of narrators linking back to the Prophet (SAW) is termed the ______
explanation: The Isnad is the sequential transmission chain of trustworthy reporters, while the Matn is the actual verbatim text of the tradition.

question: A Hadith that meets all conditions of sound transmission: continuous chain, upright narrators with flawless retentive memory, freedom from hidden defects and oddities, is classified as ______
explanation: A Sahih (sound) Hadith fulfills five rigorous criteria: connected chain (Ittisal as-Sanad), narrator integrity ('Adalah), retention (Dabt), absence of irregularity (Shadh), and absence of crippling flaw ('Illah).

question: A prophetic tradition that has been narrated by such an overwhelmingly large number of companions at every stage of transmission that collective collusion upon a lie is impossible is a ______ Hadith.
explanation: A Mutawatir tradition conveys certain knowledge because it is transmitted by a multitude of independent reporters at every generation.

question: Which two celebrated scholars authored the two most authoritative and authentic collections of Hadith, collectively revered in Sunni Islam as the 'Sahihayn'?

options.a: Imam Muhammad al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
options.b: Imam Abu Dawood and Imam at-Tirmidhi
options.c: Imam an-Nasa'i and Imam Ibn Majah
options.d: Imam Malik and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal

explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are universally acknowledged as the Sahihayn (the Two Sound Collections), holding the highest degree of canonical authority.

question: The opening Hadith in Imam an-Nawawi's Forty Hadith collection, narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), emphasizes that ______

options.a: Actions are judged according to the intentions behind them
options.b: Halal and Haram are distinctly clear
options.d: The Qur'an was revealed in seven dialects

explanation: The foundational tradition states: 'Innamal a'malu bin-niyyat' (Verily, actions are judged only by intentions, and every person will have only what they intended).

question: In the renowned 'Hadith of Jibril' (Hadith 2 of an-Nawawi), how did the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) define 'Ihsan' (spiritual perfection)?

options.a: 'To worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, know that He sees you'
options.c: 'To memorize the entire text of the Qur'an'
options.d: 'To donate half of your annual wealth to charity'

explanation: The Prophet (SAW) defined Ihsan as: 'To worship Allah as if you see Him, for even if you do not see Him, He certainly sees you'.

question: In an authentic Hadith recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim, the Prophet (SAW) stated: 'None of you truly believes until he ______'

options.a: loves for his brother what he loves for himself
options.b: builds a mosque in his hometown
options.d: performs pilgrimage twice in his lifetime

explanation: The Prophet (SAW) taught mutual empathy and selflessness: 'None of you has faith until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself'.

question: According to the Prophet's teaching in Sahih Muslim, truthfulness leads to righteousness (Al-Birr), and righteousness leads to ______
explanation: The Hadith teaches: 'Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise (Jannah), while falsehood leads to wickedness, which leads to Hellfire'.

question: When a man approached the Prophet (SAW) asking for concise advice, what counsel did the Prophet repeat three times?
explanation: A man requested: 'Counsel me', and the Prophet (SAW) answered: 'Do not get angry (La taghdab)'. He repeated this several times.

question: Belief in Allah as the sole Creator, Provider, Controller, and Sovereign Sustainer of the entire universe is the domain of ______
explanation: Tawheed ar-Rububiyyah denotes the affirmation of Allah's unique Lordship as sole Creator, Cherisher, and Sovereign Ruler of creation.

question: Directing all acts of worship, supplication (Du'a), sacrificial slaughter, and vows exclusively to Allah alone without any partner corresponds to ______
explanation: Tawheed al-Uluhiyyah (Oneness of Worship) mandates that no act of devotion, sacrifice, or prayer may be dedicated to anything or anyone other than Allah.

question: Ostentation, displaying good deeds in public worship solely to earn the praise and admiration of people (Riya'), is classified in Islam as ______
explanation: Riya' (showing off in acts of worship) is described by the Prophet (SAW) as Shirk al-Asghar (the minor polytheism), which corrupts the rewarded deed.

question: Which archangel is tasked with the divine duty of delivering heavenly revelations (Wahy) to all prophets and messengers of Allah?
explanation: Angel Jibril (AS) is the Ruh al-Qudus (Holy Spirit) and Ruh al-Amin (Trustworthy Spirit) charged with conveying divine scripture to the prophets.

question: Which two angels are commissioned to interrogate deceased persons in the grave concerning their Lord, religion, and Prophet?
explanation: Munkar and Nakir are the two angels assigned to question every individual in the grave (Barzakh).

question: Which sacred scripture was revealed to Prophet Dawud (David, AS) according to the Holy Qur'an?
explanation: Surah An-Nisa (4:163) explicitly mentions: '...and to David We gave the Zabur (Psalms)'.

question: Which of the following groups consists exclusively of the five 'Ulul 'Azm' (Prophets of Firm Determination and Inflexible Resolve) mentioned in the Qur'an?

options.a: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa, and Muhammad (PBUT)
options.b: Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, and Salih (PBUT)
options.c: Ibrahim, Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, and Yusuf (PBUT)
options.d: Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yunus, and Zakariyya (PBUT)

explanation: The five great Arch-Prophets of exceptional resolve (Ulul 'Azm) are Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus), and Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Them All).

question: The razor-sharp, perilous bridge spanning across the expanse of Hellfire over which every soul must cross on the Day of Resurrection is the ______
explanation: As-Sirat is the narrow bridge established over Jahannam which believers will cross into Paradise with varying speeds based upon their righteous deeds.

question: The ritual dry purification using clean sand or dust performed when water is unavailable or medically harmful to use is called ______
explanation: Tayammum is the symbolic, dry purification sanctioned by the Qur'an (4:43) using clean earth when water cannot be found or safely used.

question: Which of the following conditions mandates the performance of Ghusl (complete ritual bath) rather than simple Wudu?

options.a: Janabah (state of post-coital or seminal discharge)

explanation: Janabah (major ritual impurity resulting from sexual intercourse or emission of seminal fluid) obligates a full purifying bath (Ghusl).

question: The special prostration performed either before or after the Taslim to rectify accidental additions, omissions, or uncertainties in prayer is called ______
explanation: Sujud as-Sahw consists of two compensatory prostrations made to rectify errors caused by forgetfulness during Salah.

question: Which of the following uniquely distinguishes Salatul Janazah (the funeral prayer) from standard congregational prayers?

options.a: It has no Ruku' (bowing) and no Sujud (prostration), consisting solely of four Takbirs while standing
options.b: It must be prayed facing away from the Qiblah
options.c: It is obligatory only for royal dignitaries
options.d: It requires performing Wudu three consecutive times

explanation: The Islamic funeral prayer is performed entirely standing (Qiyam) with four Takbirs, containing neither bowing (Ruku') nor prostration (Sujud).

question: What is the minimum qualifying threshold of savings or wealth an individual must possess for a full lunar year before Zakah becomes obligatory?
explanation: Nisab is the specific minimum exemption limit of zakatable wealth below which no Zakah is due.

question: How many distinct categories of eligible recipients of Zakah are divinely ordained in Surah At-Tawbah (verse 60)?
explanation: Surah At-Tawbah 9:60 enumerates exactly eight categories: the poor, needy, administrators, reconciling hearts, freeing captives, debtors, in the cause of Allah, and the wayfarer.

question: The mandatory charitable contribution given by every Muslim household head on behalf of every dependent before the Eid al-Fitr prayer is ______
explanation: Zakat al-Fitr (or Sadaqat al-Fitr) is an obligatory purification levy in the form of staple food given before the morning prayer on Eid al-Fitr.

question: What is the heavy religious expiation (Kaffarah) required of a person who deliberately and without lawful excuse invalidates their Ramadan fast through sexual intercourse?

options.a: Freeing a slave, or fasting for two consecutive lunar months, or feeding sixty indigent persons
options.c: Fasting every day for an entire year
options.d: Reciting the entire Qur'an twenty times

explanation: The prescribed Kaffarah for breaking Ramadan fast via marital relations is freeing a slave, or if unable, fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty needy people.

question: Which of the following is considered the absolute core pillar of Hajj, without which the pilgrimage is entirely invalid, as affirmed by the Hadith 'Al-Hajju Arafah'?

options.a: Wuquf (standing) at Mount Arafat on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah
options.c: Drinking water from the well of Zamzam
options.d: Visiting the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah

explanation: Wuquf bi-Arafat (standing at the plains of Arafat from noon until sunset on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah) is the supreme, non-negotiable pillar of Hajj.

question: The designated geographic boundary stations where pilgrims intending to perform Hajj or Umrah must enter the sacred state of Ihram are called ______
explanation: The Mawaqit (such as Dhul-Hulayfah, Al-Juhfah, Qarn al-Manazil, Yalamlam, Dhat 'Irq) are territorial perimeter stations designated by the Prophet (SAW) for assuming Ihram.

question: Which of the following constitutes an indispensable legal condition for the validity of an Islamic marriage contract (Nikah)?

options.a: Mutual consent, the consent of the bride's guardian (Wali), two upright male witnesses, and payment of Mahr
options.b: Holding a lavish banquet in an urban hotel
options.c: Registration with a Western civil registry

explanation: A valid Nikah requires the mutual offer and acceptance (Ijab and Qabul), the presence of the bride's Wali, two trustworthy witnesses, and the specification of the dower (Mahr).

question: What is the statutory waiting period (Iddah) prescribed for a non-pregnant Muslim woman whose husband has passed away?

options.a: Four lunar months and ten days

explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:234) prescribes that widows must observe an Iddah of exactly four months and ten days.

question: The dissolution of an Islamic marriage initiated by the wife through mutual agreement in exchange for financial compensation (such as returning her Mahr) is known as ______
explanation: Khul' is a divorce proceeding initiated by the wife wherein she returns her marriage gift (Mahr) or gives monetary settlement to release herself from the marital bond.

question: In the Islamic law of inheritance (Mirath), which class of primary legal heirs can never be completely excluded from inheriting under any circumstances?

options.a: Father, mother, husband or wife, son, and daughter

explanation: The five primary heirs who never suffer total exclusion from the estate are the parents (father and mother), the surviving spouse (husband or wife), and direct children (son and daughter).

question: The severe, three-year socioeconomic boycott imposed by the pagan Quraysh against the Prophet's clan, Banu Hashim, took place in the valley known as ______
explanation: The Quraysh boycotted the Prophet (SAW) and Banu Hashim from 7 to 10 of the Prophet's mission, confining them to the arid gorge of Shi'b Abi Talib.

question: The tenth year of Prophethood is historically designated as the 'Year of Sorrow' ('Am al-Huzn) due to the deaths of which two vital protectors of the Prophet (SAW)?

options.a: His beloved wife Khadijah (RA) and his uncle Abu Talib
options.b: His uncle Hamzah and his daughter Ruqayyah
options.c: His companion Abu Bakr and his mother Aminah
options.d: His grandfather Abdul-Muttalib and his son Ibrahim

explanation: 'Am al-Huzn (Year of Sorrow) witnessed the loss of Khadijah (RA), the Prophet's emotional pillar, and Abu Talib, his political guardian against the Quraysh.

question: The historic bilateral fraternal pact instituted by the Prophet (SAW) in Madinah pairing each Meccan migrant with an indigenous Madinan helper was the ______
explanation: The Prophet (SAW) established the system of Mu'akhah (fraternal bond) between the Muhajirun (emigrants) and the Ansar (helpers) to foster absolute communal solidarity.

question: In which decisive battle fought on the 17th of Ramadan, 2 AH, did an ill-equipped force of 313 Muslims triumph over an elite Quraysh army numbering over one thousand?
explanation: The Battle of Badr was the landmark military engagement where Allah granted supernatural victory to the 313 Muslims, establishing Islam's geopolitical ascendancy.

question: Which Rightly Guided Caliph established the Islamic Hijri calendar, instituted the public treasury (Bayt al-Mal), and established administrative departments (Diwan)?
explanation: Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) was an administrative genius who created the Hijri era dated from the Hijrah, organized the Diwan, judicial system, and military garrisons.

question: The renowned 14th-century ruler of the Mali Empire whose lavish 1324 pilgrimage to Makkah distributed so much gold in Cairo that it devalued the metal's price for over a decade was ______
explanation: Mansa Kankan Musa performed a legendary Hajj in 1324 with a caravan carrying immense quantities of gold, placing Mali conspicuously on medieval European cartographic maps.
